reason: Both phase timing boundaries and last-turn-step restriction with specified exceptions resolved.

question.question: What do at-start and at-end phase timings mean, and can you take ordinary Daylight actions after beginning the last step of your turn?

expected.expected_answer: Start happens before all other phase effects; end after other phase effects but before next phase. Once last turn step begins no actions except explicitly end-of-Evening or end-of-turn actions.

source_passages.quotation: Take turns clockwise: **Birdsong → Daylight → Evening**. “At start” effects precede all other phase effects; “at end” effects follow everything else in that phase, before next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions. An action, ability or persistent effect cannot be interrupted unless an effect explicitly permits it; a Marquise March's two moves are one compound action. If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. For battle effects at the same timing, attacker chooses their order. (1.1.3, 1.4, 4.3.)

answer.ruling: At-start effects happen before all other effects of that phase. At-end effects happen after everything else in that phase and before the next phase.
Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions may be taken unless they are explicitly end-of-Evening or end-of-turn actions.
